newsitem.title: ZAIRE: New Zaire premier earmarks ministries for rebels.
newsitem.headline: New Zaire premier earmarks ministries for rebels.

text.p: Zaire's new prime minister, Etienne Tshisekedi, unveiled a government on Thursday with no representatives of veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko and six ministries earmarked for Laurent Kabila's rebels.

Tshisekedi, who announced details of the 26-member government at a news conference, said the portfolios of foreign affairs, defence, budget, planning, foreign trade and agriculture were reserved for the rebel alliance.

Tshisekedi, who has never accepted his 1993 sacking from the post by Mobutu, also announced the dissolution of Zaire's transitional parliament and the revival of the sovereign national conference that launched Zaire's democratic transition.
It was not immediately clear whether he had the authority to do this.
The national conference dissolved itself in December 1992 to make way for a High Council of the Republic, which in turn evolved into the transitional parliament in 1994.
The transitional parliament nominated Tshisekedi on Tuesday after Kengo wa Dondo, who was appointed in 1994 and had strongly backed the military option in the war, resigned.
Mobutu ratified the appointment of Tshisekedi, a veteran opponent who has called for talks with the rebels from early in the conflict, on Wednesday.

Tshisekedi's government is essentially the same as the one that he led when Mobutu sacked him. That government included no members of Mobutu's Popular Revolutionary Movement (MPR), who hold a majority in the transitional parliament.
Tshisekedi was originally appointed by the national conference in 1991.

Mobutu, who has cancer, has seen his grip on the sprawling Central African nation weakened by rebel advances. The rebels took up arms in October in a dispute over Zairean nationality for ethnic Tutsis. They say Mobutu must stand down.
Representatives of the rebels and Zaire's divided political family are due to meet in South Africa this week to launch peace talks.
